title: What is Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Data Factory is Fabric's data integration workload: it connects to data sources, moves data, transforms it, and orchestrates movement and transformation tasks from a single place, with connectivity to more than 170 data sources spanning cloud, multicloud, and on-premises systems reached through gateways.

Microsoft positions Data Factory in Fabric as the next generation of Azure Data Factory, and publishes a comparison guide plus a migration guide for moving Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse pipelines into Fabric.

Data Factory offers three distinct data-movement options: Copy job for simplified movement with built-in delivery styles (bulk, incremental, and change-data-capture replication), Copy activity for fully customizable movement with manual control of parallelism, and Mirroring for near-real-time database replication into OneLake.

Mirroring is surfaced from Data Factory as a data-movement method that keeps a near-real-time replica of an operational database inside OneLake, so analytics and reporting can run against the replica instead of the source system.

Dataflow Gen2 is Data Factory's low-code transformation surface, offering over 300 transformations including joins, aggregations, data cleansing, and custom logic, and is the tool Microsoft recommends when data must be shaped before it is loaded (classic ETL).

Fabric Data Factory deliberately supports both ETL and ELT in the same solution: shape data in Dataflow Gen2 before loading when quality and standardization matter up front, or land raw data first and push transformation down to Spark notebooks or SQL engines over OneLake for large cloud-scale datasets.

Pipelines are the orchestration layer: a single pipeline can chain data movement, transformation activities (Fabric notebooks, Spark job definitions, HDInsight, stored procedures, SQL scripts, dbt jobs), and control-flow constructs such as loops and conditionals, all authored in a low-code designer.
Teams that prefer code-first orchestration can use Data Factory's Apache Airflow integration to express workflows as Python DAGs instead of the visual pipeline designer.
dbt jobs in Fabric Data Factory run SQL-based dbt model transformations directly against a Fabric data warehouse, with a no-code setup for building, testing, and deploying the models.

Copilot for Data Factory lets users author and edit pipelines and dataflows from natural-language prompts, summarizes what existing dataflow queries and pipelines do, and explains run errors with suggested fixes.

A practical division of labor in Fabric data integration: use pipelines when the problem is orchestration and large-scale movement, use Dataflow Gen2 when the problem is low-code data shaping, and consult Microsoft's data-movement decision guide to choose between Copy job, Copy activity, and Mirroring for a given scenario.
